title: Configurable DSP-Based CAM Architecture for Data-Intensive Applications on FPGAs
problem: FPGA-based Content-Addressable Memory (CAM) implementations suffer from high LUT/BRAM resource utilization, limited scalability, and suboptimal performance due to inefficient parallel search operations.
method: Novel DSP-block-based CAM architecture leverages digital signal processing blocks' built-in storage and logic capabilities as the core resource. DSP blocks efficiently implement parallel content search and multi-query support. Configuration parameters allow application-specific tuning of CAM width, depth, and search parallelism.

title: Tally: Non-Intrusive Performance Isolation for Concurrent Deep Learning Workloads
problem: GPU sharing for concurrent deep learning workloads suffers from high interference between co-running jobs, causing up to 188.9% latency overhead on high-priority inference tasks. Existing GPU sharing mechanisms impose high integration costs, offer inadequate performance isolation, and have limited application compatibility.
method: Tally implements a non-intrusive GPU sharing mechanism based on fine-grained thread-block-level kernel scheduling. It intercepts GPU kernel launches and dynamically schedules thread blocks across co-running workloads without requiring application modification, allowing the system to control interference between high-priority inference and best-effort training tasks at the thread-block granularity rather than at the kernel or process level.

title: HardHarvest: Hardware-Supported Core Harvesting for Microservices
problem: Software core harvesting—where batch 'Harvest VMs' temporarily steal idle cores from latency-critical 'Primary VMs'—incurs prohibitive overheads (hypervisor calls, TLB/cache flushes, context switches) that are acceptable for monolithic applications but intolerable for sub-millisecond microservices.
method: HardHarvest implements core harvesting entirely in hardware by adding in-hardware request scheduling logic that detects idle cores in Primary VMs and assigns them to Harvest VM tasks without hypervisor intervention. TLBs and caches are partitioned between Primary and Harvest VMs using a smart replacement algorithm that protects Primary VM working sets, enabling rapid context transfer without full TLB/cache flushes. The hardware scheduler monitors Primary VM request queues and preempts Harvest VM work before Primary VM tail latency is impacted.

title: EPOC: An Efficient Pulse Generation Framework with Advanced Synthesis for Quantum Circuits
problem: Quantum optimal control has high computational overhead and generates long circuit latencies; gate-based pulse generation requires substantial resource overhead.
method: EPOC combines ZX-Calculus, circuit partitioning, and advanced circuit synthesis for efficient pulse generation. The approach implements finer granularity in pulse generation and explores equivalent circuit representations to increase parallelism. ZX-Calculus enables compact circuit abstraction and optimization, while partitioning allows parallel processing of circuit segments.

title: High-throughput Point-Cloud Accelerator with Sparsity-aware Hierarchical Neighbor Voxel Search and Skipping
problem: 3D sparse convolution networks for point cloud processing face challenges from irregular voxel sparsity patterns, increasing hardware complexity and reducing efficiency when exploiting sparsity.
method: Algorithm-hardware co-design approach combining on-the-fly threshold-based voxel skipping at the algorithm level with a hierarchical 3-stage Voxel Search and Skipping engine at the hardware level to systematically narrow down the non-zero search space and adapt to irregular sparsity.

title: ARCANE: Adaptive RISC-V Cache Architecture for Near-memory Extensions
problem: Von Neumann architectures suffer from data movement bottlenecks (extensive memory traffic, low throughput, poor energy efficiency). Existing accelerators improve performance but lack flexibility and require explicit data transfers; compute in-/near-memory solutions face usability challenges due to data placement constraints.
method: ARCANE integrates a tightly-coupled compute-near-memory coprocessor into the cache hierarchy via a RISC-V cache controller. The controller executes custom instructions from the host CPU using vector operations dispatched to near-memory vector processing units embedded within cache memory. Software-transparent synchronization and data mapping are automatically handled by the architecture.

title: PIMnet: A Domain-Specific Network for Efficient Collective Communication in Scalable PIM
problem: PIM compute units can only access their local memory; inter-bank communication in PIM systems must route through the host CPU, which becomes a bottleneck for collective communication operations (e.g., all-reduce, broadcast) that are common in many workloads, limiting PIM's scalability.
method: PIMnet is a PIM-controlled interconnection network providing direct connectivity between PIM compute units across banks and chips, bypassing the host CPU. It exploits bandwidth parallelism by allowing concurrent inter-bank and inter-chip communication. The network topology matches the DRAM packaging hierarchy with a multi-tier architecture (intra-chip and inter-chip tiers). Unlike traditional network-on-chip designs, PIMnet is managed by the PIM logic itself, not the host, to minimize hardware overhead and optimize collective communication patterns.

title: SSDTrain: An Activation Offloading Framework to SSDs for Faster Large Language Model Training
problem: GPU memory capacity growth lags LLM size growth; activations (intermediate tensors from forward pass) dominate GPU memory use during training, limiting micro-batch size and increasing training overhead through expensive weight updates.
method: SSDTrain adaptively offloads activations to high-capacity NVMe SSDs while fully overlapping data transfers with computation, employing tensor deduplication and forwarding optimizations, and integrating with PyTorch, Megatron, and DeepSpeed frameworks.

title: 31.1 An Inductor-Less Capacitor-Less Synchronous Piezoelectric-Electromagnetic Hybrid Energy Harvesting Platform with Coil-Sharing Scheme
problem: Energy harvesting for IoT and edge AI devices requires multiple discrete or on-chip power components (inductors, capacitors) across rectification, DC-DC conversion, and regulation stages, increasing system volume, cost, and area.
method: Hybrid piezoelectric (PE) and electromagnetic (EM) energy harvesting platform that reuses the EM harvester's inherent coil as an inductor across ALL stages (rectification, DC-DC, regulation) instead of requiring separate off-chip inductors or capacitors, using a coil-sharing synchronous rectification scheme.

title: Graph in the Vault: Protecting Edge GNN Inference with Trusted Execution Environment
problem: GNN model intellectual property and private graph data are vulnerable during edge deployment; existing defenses do not adequately protect both model parameters and graph topology against extraction and privacy attacks.
method: GNNVault partitions GNNs into a public backbone model and a private GNN rectifier component, both protected within Intel SGX trusted execution environment compartments, securing both model parameters and graph data during inference without requiring full model deployment in TEE.

title: MoC-System: Efficient Fault Tolerance for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts Model Training
problem: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) LLMs have model parameter counts far exceeding dense models of equivalent compute cost, making checkpoint-based fault tolerance extremely expensive in terms of checkpoint size, write bandwidth, and recovery time for distributed training at >10k node scale.
method: MoC-System exploits the sparse activation pattern of MoE models: only a subset of experts is activated per token, so most expert parameters are not updated in any given training step. The system uses a Model-on-Checkpoint (MoC) approach that selectively checkpoints only the experts that were actually updated (activated) during a training step, avoiding checkpointing dormant expert parameters. This is combined with distributed checkpoint orchestration to overlap checkpoint I/O with forward/backward computation and expert-parallel sharding to minimize per-node checkpoint volume.

title: Symbiotic Task Scheduling and Data Prefetching
problem: Hardware task-parallel systems that operate with fine-grained tasks (approx. 100-cycle execution time) cannot benefit from conventional hardware prefetchers because tasks are too short for prefetches to complete before the task finishes, leaving DRAM latency fully exposed and undermining the performance gains of hardware task management.
method: The Task-Seeded Prefetcher (TSP) learns the data-access pattern of each task function type and issues prefetches as soon as a task descriptor is queued by the hardware task scheduler, using the descriptor as a seed to identify which memory addresses the task will access. The Memory Response Task Scheduler (MRS) augments the baseline task-to-core dispatch policy by monitoring prefetch completion status from TSP: when a task's prefetches are done, MRS preferentially dispatches it to a ready core, maximizing prefetch utilization without stalling the pipeline. Together, TSP and MRS form a symbiotic pair where scheduling drives prefetching and prefetch status informs scheduling.

title: Anchor First, Accelerate Next: Revolutionizing GNNs with PIM by Harnessing Stationary Data
problem: Graph neural network processing on PIM architectures suffers from cross-bank data movement; only 35.6% of data stays stationary within PIM units on average, degrading efficiency as PIM density increases.
method: Anchor architecture uses hardware-software co-design. Software-level Mastav graph partitioning algorithm allocates vertices and edges to maximize stationary data within PIM banks. Hardware-level customized dataflow ensures non-stationary data is accessed and distributed exactly once. An optimized communication mechanism reduces redundant transfers through critical path analysis.

title: ACRS: Adjacent Computation Resource Sharing among Partitioned GPU Sub-Cores
problem: Modern GPU sub-core partitioning reduces power and area but prevents task distribution across sub-cores; functional units (FUs) frequently stall waiting for results while adjacent sub-cores have unoccupied FUs, wasting compute capacity.
method: ACRS framework enables dynamic sharing of functional units among adjacent sub-cores through two modules: Shared FU Issue (SF_ISSUE) monitors operand collector and FU status, offloading stalled instructions to unoccupied FUs in adjacent sub-cores; Shared FU Write Back (SF_WriteBack) routes results back. Fixed target core assignment minimizes wiring overhead.

title: FLEXPROF: Flexible, Side-Channel-Free Memory Access
problem: Secure memory controllers that prevent microarchitectural side-channels by allocating fixed 'turns' to co-scheduled VMs impose a ~2x performance slowdown because the schedule must conservatively handle worst-case mixed read/write patterns, leaving memory bus utilization inefficient.
method: FlexProf introduces two types of memory controller turns: read-optimized turns and write-optimized turns, selected via coarse-grain application profiling that observes the read/write ratio without leaking sensitive information. Each turn type is sized and structured for its dominant operation. Flexibility is added so that a read-optimized turn can opportunistically issue writes when read slots are idle (and vice versa), improving utilization while preserving the fixed-turn structure needed to prevent timing side-channels between VMs.

title: 8.5 A Command-Aware Hybrid LDO for Advanced HBM Interfaces with 150μA Quiescent Current and 20pF On-Chip Capacitor Achieving Sub-10mV Voltage Droop in 400ps Settling Time
problem: HBM3E/HBM4 interfaces suffer from power-supply-induced jitter (PSIJ) caused by sudden load current surges in write-data-strobe (WDQS) buffers, leading to voltage droop and sampling errors in high-bandwidth memory.
method: A command-aware hybrid LDO uses predictive techniques triggered by command signals (ACT_CMD) to mitigate voltage droop before WDQS buffer transients occur, achieving sub-10mV droop with minimal on-chip capacitance (20pF) and low quiescent current (150μA).
